top_story: Iran’s mass funeral for Ali Khamenei on 6 July turned public mourning over his killing in the February US-Israeli strikes into a potent display of national grievance, reinforcing the domestic pressure behind Tehran’s confrontational posture. Within a day, that tension spilled into the Gulf as attacks on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz triggered direct US strikes on Iran, sharply widening the risk to shipping, energy flows, and civilian livelihoods across the region. In Gaza, Hamas’s move to dissolve its government and accept a US-backed interim administration for civilian affairs signals tactical flexibility under wartime strain, but its refusal to disarm preserves the core coercive dispute. The regional picture is hardening into parallel tracks of escalation and improvised governance, with military retaliation deepening insecurity even as political actors seek narrow mechanisms to manage collapse.
